title: Website Design Cost: $12 a Month Builder vs a Developer
desc: A website builder plan costs $12 to $39 a month; a developer earns a $44.54 an hour median wage. Published prices from Squarespace, Wix, Shopify and Webflow.
keywords: website design cost, web design cost, website development cost, ecommerce website cost, cost of a website, small business website cost, squarespace pricing, wix pricing, shopify pricing, webflow pricing, how much does a website cost
cta: Want a written fixed-price quote for your website?
body:
Short answer. A website you build yourself on a hosted builder costs about $12 to $39 a month on the entry and mid plans: Squarespace lists Basic at $12 a month on annual billing, Webflow lists Basic at $15, Wix lists Light at $17, and Shopify lists Basic at $22 for a store. Paying a person to design and build it costs their time, and the most reliable published number for that time is the US median wage of $92,650 a year for web developers and $104,000 for web and digital interface designers in May 2025, which is about $44.54 and $50.00 an hour in wages alone. All prices below were read on the vendors' own pages on 9 November 2026.

Three ways to pay for a website

Almost every small business site is built one of three ways, and each one charges for a different thing.

A hosted builder. You pay a subscription and do the design work yourself from templates. The subscription covers hosting, the editor and usually a domain for the first year. The cost is a monthly or yearly fee, plus your own hours.

A freelancer or agency. You pay for someone's hours, or a fixed project fee that is built from their hours. You still usually pay a platform fee on top if the site runs on a builder or a store platform.

A custom build. A developer writes the site or the app for you. The cost is almost entirely labour, and it recurs when you want changes.

The useful question is therefore not "what does a website cost" but "which of these three bills do I want to carry". The rest of this guide prices the first one from published plans and the second one from published wages, and says plainly where no published price exists.

What the builders publish

We read each plan on the vendor's own page. Prices change, and some vendors show a different number for annual and monthly billing, so the billing period is in the table.

Builder and planPublished priceBillingWhat the page says
Squarespace Basic$12 a monthAnnual (monthly billing: $19)Free custom domain, up to 2 contributors, 2% online store fee
Squarespace Core$17 a monthAnnual (monthly billing: $27)Marked Recommended, unlimited contributors, 0% online store fee
Squarespace Advanced$25 a monthAnnual (monthly billing: $36)0% online store fee, advanced commerce tools
Wix Light$17 a monthYearly, paid in fullFree domain for 1 year, 2 GB storage, 2 collaborators
Wix Core$29 a monthYearly, paid in full50 GB storage, accept payments, basic eCommerce
Wix Business$39 a monthYearly, paid in fullMarked Recommended, 100 GB, standard eCommerce
Webflow Basic$15 a monthBilled yearlyFor simple sites that don't need a CMS, 300 static pages
Webflow Premium$25 a monthBilled yearlyIncludes the Webflow CMS, listed as new
WordPress.com Personal$4 a month first term, $5 at renewalBilled every 12 months, excluding taxesList price $9 a month
WordPress.com Business$25 a month first term, $28 at renewalBilled every 12 monthsList price $40 a month

Read it as a range rather than a quote. The entry plans run from $4 to $17 a month, and the mid plans we listed run from $17 to $39. Webflow's pricing page shows its Basic and Premium plans as billed yearly, and WordPress.com's pricing page shows a lower first-term price and a higher renewal price, so the second year can cost more than the first. The Wix's plans page says its displayed prices are for yearly subscriptions paid in full at the time of purchase, so $17 a month on Wix means $204 charged once a year. The Squarespace's pricing page offers a 14-day free trial and says paying annually saves up to 36%.

If you sell products, the store platforms

A store is priced differently from a brochure site because the platform also takes a payment layer. On Shopify's pricing page, which showed US dollar prices when we read it, Basic is $25 a month billed monthly or $22 a month billed yearly, Grow is $65 or $58, and Advanced is $399 or $359. Plus starts at $2,300 a month. Shopify lists a 3-day free trial and an option to extend it for US$1.

Over a year, that is $264 for Shopify Basic on yearly billing and $300 on monthly billing. The WordPress.com Commerce plan, also on WordPress.com's pricing page, lists $70 a month, $45 for the first term and $50 at renewal, which is $600 a year after the first term. Squarespace Advanced and Wix Business both include store features at $300 and $468 a year on the billing the pages show for them.

What a year on each entry plan adds up to

Multiplying the monthly price by 12 gives the yearly bill. These are our own sums from the published prices, before taxes and before any add-on such as email, apps or a premium theme.

What a developer's time costs

We did not find an agency or freelancer price list from a primary source, so we cannot give you "the" cost of a custom site. What is published is what these workers are paid. The Bureau of Labor Statistics Occupational Outlook Handbook lists a median annual wage of $92,650 for web developers and $104,000 for web and digital interface designers in May 2025. Dividing by 2,080 working hours a year gives about $44.54 and $50.00 an hour.

That is a wage, not a billing rate. A freelancer or an agency adds tax, overhead, unbilled time and profit, so a price you are quoted should be higher than the wage. It is still a useful floor for the arithmetic.

Here is a hypothetical. If a simple site took 80 hours of work, a figure we picked for illustration and not one taken from a source, that is $3,563 at the developer median wage and $4,000 at the designer median wage, before any overhead or profit. Against a Squarespace Core plan at $204 a year, $3,563 equals about 17.5 years of subscription. Against Shopify Basic at $264 a year, it equals about 13.5 years.

The gap is real, but it does not make the builder the better buy in every case. It tells you what the extra money has to be buying.

When a builder wins and when custom wins

These are our opinions, not findings from a source.

A builder tends to win when the site is a handful of pages, the layout can come from a template, you can write and edit the content yourself, and you do not need logic the platform does not offer. The money goes to the subscription, and you can change things the same day.

Paying for a developer tends to win when the site has to do something the builder cannot, such as a custom booking flow, a connection to your CRM or an unusual checkout, when speed and structure matter enough to justify custom code, or when you have no time to do the design yourself and the hours are worth more to you than the fee. It also matters when you want the code and the hosting under your control instead of renting them.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics notes that improving web development tools and increasing use of AI for web development may soften employment growth for these workers, because the tools can make them more productive and let some workers in other occupations do basic web development tasks. For a buyer, that is one more reason to be wary of a quote that prices a basic template site as if it were custom engineering.

What a website quote should itemize

Whoever you hire, we suggest asking for the price in writing, broken into these lines, so you can compare two quotes on the same terms.

Design and build. The number of pages or templates, the number of revision rounds, and who writes the content.

Platform and hosting. Which builder or hosting you will be on, who owns the account, and what the monthly or yearly fee is. Compare it with the plan prices above.

Integrations. Forms, payments, CRM, email and analytics, each priced separately.

After launch. Who fixes things, who updates the site, and what that costs per hour or per month.

Ownership. Whether you receive the domain, the files and the logins when the project ends.

For related price breakdowns, see our guide to app development cost and, if your store needs custom code, Shopify app development cost.

We suggest asking any provider, us included, for a written quote that follows the checklist above, so you can see what you are paying for before you start.

This guide uses published prices read on 9 November 2026. Plans change, so check the vendor's page before you buy.
faqs: How much does a website cost?

It depends on the route. A hosted builder lists entry plans from $12 a month on Squarespace (annual billing), $15 on Webflow and $17 on Wix, and plans that take payments run to $29 or $39 a month on Wix. A developer's time is priced differently: the US median wage was $92,650 a year for web developers in May 2025, about $44.54 an hour in wages before any agency overhead or profit.
How much does a small business website cost per year?

On the entry plans, between about $144 and $264 a year, from our arithmetic on published prices: Squarespace Basic $144, Webflow Basic $180, Wix Light $204 and Shopify Basic on yearly billing $264. That is before taxes, add-ons and your own time. A custom build adds labour on top.
Is it cheaper to build a website yourself?

In cash, usually yes: the subscriptions above cost a few hundred dollars a year, while 80 hypothetical hours at the US median developer wage is about $3,563. But you spend your own hours, and the cheaper route only works if the template and the platform's features fit what you need.
How much does an ecommerce website cost?

On Shopify's pricing page, Basic is $25 a month on monthly billing or $22 on yearly billing, Grow is $65 or $58, and Advanced is $399 or $359. Plus starts at $2,300 a month. WordPress.com's Commerce plan lists $70 a month, with a $45 first-term price and a $50 renewal price.
Why do website quotes vary so much?

Because the price is mostly labour, and the amount of labour depends on pages, features, integrations and revision rounds. We did not find a primary source that publishes a standard agency price list, so ask each provider to itemize design, platform, integrations, support and ownership in writing.
What is the difference between web design cost and web development cost?

Design is the look and structure of the site, and development is making it work, including code, integrations and hosting. The Bureau of Labor Statistics lists them as separate occupations: web and digital interface designers, with a $104,000 median wage in May 2025, and web developers, with $92,650.
